title: Move Zeroes to End
statement:
Given an integer array `nums`, move all `0`'s to the end of it in-place while maintaining the relative order of the non-zero elements.

Note that you must do this in-place without making a copy of the array.

examples.explanation: Moving the two zeroes to the end yields [1, 3, 12, 0, 0].

editorial.approach: Use a two-pointer approach. Keep track of the position of the last non-zero element using `lastNonZeroFoundAt`. Iterate through the array. When a non-zero element is found, swap it with the element at `lastNonZeroFoundAt` and increment `lastNonZeroFoundAt`.

hints: You can use a two-pointer approach here.
Keep a pointer `lastNonZeroAt` at 0. Iterate `i` through the array.

bruteForceSolution.explanation: Create a temporary array, push all non-zero elements, fill the rest with zeroes, and copy them back into the original array.

optimizedSolution.explanation: Maintain a slow pointer `lastNonZeroAt`. Scan the array with a fast pointer. Swap non-zero elements into the slow pointer position, bubble-shifting zeroes to the right.

interviewExplanation: Instead of allocating O(n) memory to push non-zero elements, we use a two-pointer partitioning approach (similar to QuickSort's partition). One pointer tracks the boundary of non-zero elements and the other scans, swapping elements in-place in O(n) time and O(1) space.
